title: Route Prism: Per-model & Per-route Performance Dashboard Spec
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Deliver a compact but expressive per-route and per-model performance dashboard (Route Prism) that surfaces latency distributions, throughput, token-level cost attribution, and rollout-aware comparisons. The UI must support three common personas: product engineers (latency & regressions), platform operators (SLOs & capacity), and finance/ops (cost allocation).

This ticket covers: detailed chart specs, interaction patterns for drilldowns, rollout diffing mode (two-model comparison across the same route), and a responsive compact layout for single-panel embeds in the route list. The aim is to replace ad-hoc charts with a single coherent view that answers the 4 core questions: 1) Is latency meeting SLOs? 2) Where are tokens expended (prompt vs. generation vs. tools)? 3) Are rollouts introducing regressions? 4) What is the cost-per-1000-token trend and which model variants drive it?
acceptance_criteria:
1) Wireframes and annotated specs for desktop and compact mobile width exist in Figma and are linked.
2) Chart spec CSVs (series names, units, aggregations) attached.
3) Interaction flows for 'rollout diff' and 'time-range sync' documented.
4) A11y contrast checks and keyboard flows documented.
5) At least two engineering-run usability feedback sessions completed and notes incorporated.
6) Engineering sign-off on feasible token-level data availability and query cost implications.
decisions:
1) Use 'token-ripple' stacked area for prompt vs generation vs tools rather than stacked bars to better show token peaks over time.
2) Latency distribution will default to P50/P95/P99 violin + sparkline for trend; full CDF optional in advanced view.
3) Cost attribution panel will use model-tiered unit rates and show cost-per-route and per-model variant; we will not attempt to infer external cloud costs in v1.
4) Rollout diff mode will present two vertical panes (baseline vs candidate) with synchronized time ranges and a delta lane that highlights statistically significant regressions (t-test threshold configurable).
5) Compact embed will collapse token legend into hover tooltip and show a condensed latency microtrace sparkline.
open_questions:
1) Can backend provide token-level breakdowns at 1-min granularity for 90 days without prohibitive storage costs? (Engineering to confirm).
2) How should we represent cached tokens (prefix cache hits) in cost attribution — as lower-cost tokens or excluded?
3) What default significance threshold should we use for rollout regressions (p < 0.05 suggested)?
4) Should the cost panel default to USD or a normalized 'cost units' for teams with internal billing?
review_notes:
2025-02-14: Maya - loves the token-ripple concept but requested an explicit legend color ordering to avoid ambiguity when multiple variants are present.
2025-02-16: Julian - flagged query cost risk for 1-min granularity; suggested 5-min default with optional 1-min window for on-demand deep-dive. Engineering follow-up assigned.
2025-02-18: Renee - asked for clearer language in the rollout delta lane explaining statistical methods for non-statisticians. Added microcopy draft.
2025-02-19: PM review (Elliot Singh) - asked to prioritize a compact single-line 'cost rate' metric for finance users in the header.
implementation_notes:
- Frontend: implement charting using our chart library with custom stacked area renderer for token-ripple; add optional simplified canvas renderer for large series.
- Backend: expose aggregated series: tokens_prompt, tokens_gen, tokens_tool, cache_hits, cost_estimate_usd, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, requests_per_min. Support 'compare' API that returns baseline+candidate timeseries aligned.
- Telemetry: add tags for model_variant, route_id, rollout_id.
- Performance constraints: default retention/aggregation window 90d at 5-min granularity; 1-min on demand by scoped query (audit-logged).
